stages.S1: Textbook 5: Mrs Binta introduces Aishatu's pretend tea-shop cup problem from the classroom blackboard, four seated children facing her; each of the four friends needs a cup. The board hint Touch one. Say one number. motivates the counting method without numerals.
stages.S2: Textbook 5: We will count, read, write and order one to five. Numerals are not required before concrete modelling.
stages.S3: Textbook 6: Mrs Binta touches three cups once each, says one/two/three and states the total; textbook 7 links exact sets 1-5 to numerals and models two cups/two circles. Textbook 9 and adult 18 require live numeral formation before workbook tracing.
stages.S4: Textbook 6-7: Aishatu slows down, Grace checks, pupils touch/count with the teacher, and John asks whether a drawing can represent a cup. Adult 18 requires real-cup enactment and guided turns.
stages.S5: Textbook 8-9 / workbook 2-4: all six source tasks independently count 3/5 cups, draw 2 circles, write 1-5, show 4 and demonstrate counting once. Workbook has local diagrams and ample response spaces; exercise-book alternatives are explicit.
stages.S6: Textbook 9 / workbook 4: recall Mrs Binta before looking back; show four, then explain/show how to avoid Adamu's repeat count on a three-cup set.
stages.S7: Textbook 9 and adult 18: smaller step uses two real cups moved aside once per number word, then a fresh small set; adult guidance also separates total, numeral recognition/reading and formation difficulties.
stages.S8: Textbook 10 / adult 19: four portraits and four exact cup drawings give each friend a cup; enact this pairing with real cups before the closing dialogue opens the shop.
stages.S9: Textbook 10 / workbook 5 / adult 18-19: adult-selected 1-5 physical set and drawing; shuffled numeral recognition followed by separate mixed-order numeral naming without giving the value. Another-day fresh two-or-five-object total and shuffled recognition supplied.

stages.S1: Six-to-nine TB1: Mr Aliyu leads four seated children at the blackboard. Aishatu box-game pieces are mixed; four groups of 6/7/8/9 must be sorted, counted and checked before the game begins.
stages.S2: TB1: We will count, read, write and order six to nine. Board hint Count each one. Check the group. uses prerequisite-appropriate words.
stages.S3: TB2-3 exact counter models: 6 is 5 and 1, 7 is 5 and 2, 8 is 5 and 3, 9 is 5 and 4; names linked to numerals. TB4 live formation; TB5 sorting 6 round/7 square; TB6 real 6/7 pairing and before/after; TB7 two counters/two dots.
stages.S4: TB2-5/WB1: make and count 6, then 7, then 8 and 9; scatter without changing quantity; name mixed cards; air-write, trace and cover. Physically sort 8 triangles/9 non-square rectangles with support. Grace retries a smudge; Aishatu waits to help.
stages.S5: TB5-7/WB2-5: S002 independently sorts all 30 actual pieces, counts and orders groups. Q1 after 6=7; Q2 before 9=8; Q3 order 6,7,8,9; Q4 six dots; Q5 nine objects once each; Q6 check eight. Needed diagrams local; real materials explicit.
stages.S6: TB7/WB4: remember the method before looking back; explain and show how to check 8. John explains moving each counted piece after the pupil first attempt.
stages.S7: TB7/WB4/adult TB9: counted/uncounted mats, five plus one to model six, then independently count a fresh seven set. Sort two small groups before rebuilding target groups; air-write/trace one numeral, cover and dictate; later change order.
stages.S8: TB8: actually sort, count and arrange all 30 pieces into 6 round, 7 square, 8 triangle and 9 non-square rectangle groups before closure. Displayed groups follow increasing row order. All four children check and share turns before starting the game.
stages.S9: TB8/WB6/adult TB9-10: fresh scattered groups 8/9; S003 counts nine and independently names all shuffled 1-9 cards, with recognition 6-9 separate. Cover prior handwritten count answers, all cards and earlier numerals before S004 dictation 8,6,9,7. Delayed count 6/7/8, read 9/6/8/7, dictate 9/7/6/8, order 8/6/9 as 6/8/9, sort 7 tops/9 leaves.
